Q1: What should the guard do when it finds a Git write inside a shell wrapper (`bash -c`, `sh -c`, `eval`, `$(...)`, backticks)?
Choices:
A. Parse a literal inline script (`bash -c '<literal>'`) and run the normal merged-PR check on it, so a push to a merged PR's branch is blocked as usual. When the script can't be read safely (`eval "$x"`, variables, nested substitution that mentions `git`), ask for confirmation, the way the guard already handles an unparsed `env` wrapper. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Always ask for confirmation when a wrapper's text mentions `git` together with `push` or `commit`, without parsing the inner script.
C. Hard-block (exit 2) any wrapped Git commit or push and tell the agent to run Git directly.
**Note:** C will also block legitimate wrapped commits on unmerged branches.
Q2: Which wrapper forms are in scope?
Choices:
A. Shell `-c` interpreters (`bash`, `sh`, `zsh`, `dash`, including absolute paths), `eval`, and command substitution / backticks. These are the forms the finding names. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Everything in A, plus prefix wrappers: `sudo`, `command`, `exec`, `nohup`, `time`, `nice`, `timeout`, `xargs git ...`.
C. Only shell `-c` interpreters, which is the exact exploit in the finding.
Q3: How should the live `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` stay identical to its template, given that pipeline editors can't write `.claude/hooks/**` and CI never prepares security hooks for the parity test?
Choices:
A. The PR changes only the template (and its tests). A maintainer copies the change to the live hook by hand in the same PR before merge. The PR body flags this as a required manual step. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Let the parity test fail on the PR and rely on the post-merge `sync-claude-live-copies.yml` held draft PR for a human to merge afterwards.
C. Add the hook to `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json` temporarily.
**Note:** C weakens the parity guarantee for a security hook, so it is not advised.
